- `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION, CORRECTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Defines six fundamental epistemic states with explicit non-linear transition examples (CLAIMED->REJECTED possible; CLAIMED->SUPPORTED does not entail SUPPORTED->VERIFIED) and a 'crucial mathematical correction' rejecting a fake truth-ladder ordering in favor of a multi-argument function; notes a claim can be well-supported without being deterministically verified, and vice versa for structural properties vs business rationale." - `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION, INVARIANT] scope=OBJECT — "Elevates KnowledgeClaim (not bare Knowledge) as the central object, with a detailed schema, and states the constitutional distinction KnowledgeClaim ≠ Fact." (anchor: "KnowledgeClaim{claimId,proposition,subject,context,epistemicStatus,provenance,authorityReference,evidenceReferences,derivation,validity,version}. KnowledgeClaim ≠ Fact — preserve TruthStatus separately from EpistemicStatus.")
- `[S1060]` types=[INVARIANT, EXAMPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Restates and strengthens TRUE≠KNOWN with formal examples (something true but unknown, something believed but false), calling Truth/Belief/Knowledge/Evidence-as-distinct-dimensions 'one of the most important constitutional principles'; gives a worked coherent example (TruthStatus=UNKNOWN, EpistemicStatus=SUPPORTED, AuthorityStatus=NOT_AUTHORITATIVE, VerificationStatus=NOT_VERIFIED); applies this to AI: AIOutput->KnowledgeClaim does not imply KnowledgeClaim->AuthoritativeRule, since an LLM-generated claim ('the architecture requires X') must be distinguishable from an authoritative architectural rule." (anchor: "TRUE ∧ UNKNOWN. BELIEVED ∧ ¬TRUE. Truth, Belief, Knowledge, Evidence are distinct dimensions. KnowledgeClaim{TruthStatus, EpistemicStatus, AuthorityStatus, VerificationStatus} — four independent status dimensions, not one.")
- `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Elevates Provenance from metadata to a core architectural concept, formalizes it as a graph, and worked forward (Principle->Decision->Rule->Implementation->Observation->Evidence->Verification) and reverse (Finding->Evidence->...->Architecture Decision) traversal paths giving bidirectional traceability." (anchor: "G_P=(V,E), V={Source,Claim,Interpretation,Derivation,Decision,Observation,Evidence,Verification}, E={derivedFrom,interpretedFrom,observedBy,supportedBy,verifiedBy,approvedBy,supersedes,contextualizes,transmittedThrough}. A claim has not merely an ID; it has a history.")
- `[S1060]` types=[DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Draws an explicit three-way terminology distinction that must not collapse." (anchor: "Provenance (lineage of represented knowledge) ≠ Ownership (who owns the artifact/responsibility) ≠ Authority (who has legitimate power to establish/approve it).")
- `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION, INVARIANT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Defines AuthorityReference (referring to an organizational body, governance role, approved policy, or external authoritative source) and formalizes Authority as scoped-and-temporal Authority(X,S,T), worked example (authoritative for Domain Architecture without being authoritative for Production Operations); states Authority ≠ Truth as another constitutional invariant preventing a dangerous category error — governance declaring a rule applicable does not mathematically prove it universally true." (anchor: "AuthorityReference{authorityId,authorityType,authorityScope,effectivePeriod,sourceReference} rather than embedding a person as authority. Authority(X,S,T) — meaningless without scope S and time T. Authority ≠ Truth — GovernanceValidity ≠ UniversalTruth.")
- `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=OBJECT — "Strengthens the Evidence model into a five-component formula plus a detailed schema." (anchor: "Evidence = Observation + Method + Provenance + Context + Time. Evidence{evidenceId,observation,method,source,provenance,context,observedAt,validity,confidence/quality metadata} — confidence used carefully only where the method supports it.")
- `[S1060]` types=[DISTINCTION, INVARIANT, EXAMPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Restates Observation≠Interpretation with a worked three-layer example, and states the explicit analytical invariant that observed correlation (e.g. 'deployment failed') must not automatically become a causal explanation ('architecture caused the failure') without appropriate evidence and causal reasoning." (anchor: "Observation ('port 8081 listening') ≠ Interpretation ('Nexus reachable') ≠ Decision ('migration architecture can use this endpoint') — three distinct semantic layers. Observation → CausalExplanation forbidden. Correlation ≠ Causation.")
- `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION, DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Formalizes Determination precisely (more precise than 'storing an answer'), distinguishes it from Evidence, and establishes the subset relationship Verification⊆Determination while preserving semantic precision between different determination types." (anchor: "Determination = f(Claim, Evidence, Method, Context) — a conclusion reached by applying an identified method to available evidence against a defined proposition. Evidence ≠ Determination (e.g. Evidence: 'Module A imports Module B'; Determination: 'Rule R is violated'). Verification ⊆ Determination but not every determination is a verification (e.g. RiskAssessment produces a determination, not a verification).")
- `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE] scope=OBJECT — "Strengthens Conflict as a first-class schema with an explicit AI-must-surface-conflict architectural invariant, essential for AI; restates Supersession ≠ Conflict (a temporal replacement like Architecture v1.0 supersededBy v1.1 is not necessarily a contradiction)." (anchor: "Conflict{claimA,claimB,conflictType,scope,resolutionStatus} — KnowledgeOS must not silently choose one of two conflicting claims. - `[S1060]` types=[EXTENSION, INVARIANT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Extends Context=f(Subject,Task,Role,Authority,Scope) with an Interpretation function and the critical constraint that contextualization must never silently rewrite/mutate the canonical source." (anchor: "Context → Interpretation. Interpretation = f(K,C) — the same knowledge may legitimately generate different operational expressions under different contexts. - `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION, DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Strengthens DomainAction≠TechnicalExecution into a four-part Action formula and reasserts three chained non-equivalences as among the strongest existing architectural decisions." (anchor: "Action = Intent + Authorization + Execution + Effect (semantic dimensions, not necessarily one aggregate). Knowledge≠Authorization, Decision≠Permission, Permission≠Execution.")
- `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Presents the complete fifteen-stage epistemic pipeline, 'now much more complete than the model we had at Step 155.'" (anchor: "SOURCE → KNOWLEDGE → KNOWLEDGE CLAIM → PROVENANCE → CONTEXT → INQUIRY → EVIDENCE → DETERMINATION → DECISION → AUTHORIZATION → ACTION → OBSERVATION → VERIFICATION → GOVERNANCE → NEW/UPDATED KNOWLEDGE.")
- `[S1060]` types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Presents the formal mathematical closed-loop KnowledgeOS feedback system across ten variables (Knowledge, Inquiry, Context, Evidence, Determination, Decision, Action, Observation, Verification, Governance)." - `[S1060]` types=[CONSTRAINT, PRINCIPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "States the loop must not self-authorize, giving the required governed path and the constitutional boundary distinguishing self-generation from self-authorization."
